primary_antecedent.scope: Independent uniform boundary-barrier proof, full topology and holomorphic factorization of the degenerate quotient, and intrinsic analytic and conic affine structures.

source_correspondence: The new proofs cover Corollary 26.7.8 and Theorems 26.7.10–11. Combined with the exact DCR providers, all eleven numbered Section 26.7 results are covered.

The barrier uses a uniformly normalized coordinate and an explicit rational function. Both denominator real parts have a three-quarter-delta margin, the endpoint bound is 48/25 and the central bound is 32 delta/r.

The three nested neighborhoods and the time interval have explicit scales. Both ways of leaving the middle neighborhood are handled. The homogeneous equation and every spatial derivative bound hold uniformly over the original coefficient family.

The active set is open and each collapsed class is a compact maximal zero interval. Nonnegativity gives the vanishing spatial derivative needed to prove constancy of both the coordinate and its logarithmic derivative on a class.

The real-coordinate inverse is built first. Positive time faces are then chosen on that inverse, with activity proved on each side; this avoids an unjustified common-width assumption. The two derivative formulas retain their exact signs.

The image is exactly the open region between continuous endpoint graphs. Its fibers are precisely the original zero intervals, its domain lies in the original two-sided-active set and is globally saturated, and every compact image set has compact preimage.

The induced bijection is a homeomorphism for the actual quotient topology by a closed-map argument. Compact saturated disk preimages separate distinct classes. A countable subcover and planar bases prove second countability.

Local coefficients and solutions are extended with cutoffs and a positive time rescaling before applying parameter-slice extension. Both perturbed solutions are obtained on a common strip; the quotient chart is chosen afterwards around the whole compact class.

Strict positivity of the perturbed coefficient gives an actual inverse and the exact nonzero conjugate-coordinate chain coefficient. Weak holomorphic regularity supplies the full holomorphic conclusion for the initially C1 factor.

Moving image domains contain every fixed interior compact set eventually. A compact-preimage contradiction proves uniform convergence to the unique continuous quotient factor even when the limiting fiber is an interval. Distributional passage and the exact WCR weak-regularity proof complete holomorphic descent.

Both directions of the solution characterization and both holomorphic transition directions are proved. The condition-P normal form transfers this structure to the characteristic leaf, preserving nonzero multipliers, canonical coordinates and the actual leaf topology.

On a conic leaf homogeneity makes the radial coefficient a fixed nonzero real multiple of the nonnegative factor. The signed primitive plus i log radius solves the equation. Compatibility is checked by applying the quotient theorem to this coordinate itself; no inverse-holomorphic theorem is silently assumed.

Radial invariance of a holomorphic real part forces its derivative to be real and constant. This proves all real-affine transitions and both directions of the affine-function characterization, including constant functions and possible global holonomy.

component_scope: A zero coefficient can collapse an entire characteristic interval to one point of a complex coordinate. The quotient still has genuine complex charts when there is activity on both sides of that interval. We prove this by a monotone change of real coordinate, then prove that every homogeneous solution factors holomorphically through the quotient. A separate rational construction gives uniform boundary barriers. The final application supplies the intrinsic analytic structure on reduced two-dimensional bicharacteristics and the affine structure on their conic ray quotients.
